answer: An AI agent economy resists Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to stake non-transferable compute-backed bonds: agents periodically solve verifiable delay functions tied to unique hardware enclaves, and results are aggregated at a network summit. A Sybil attacker must duplicate enclave attestations across every fake identity, but a verification lagoon monitors device fingerprints, so mass identities collapse to one ridge of physical hardware, making attack cost linear in real devices.
